statement: An older secondary-market analysis reports used H100 units traded as high as $50,000 per GPU during mid-2024 scarcity with a $25,000-$40,000 retail range from mid-2024 into early 2026, above the roughly $21,000-$28,000 asking prices seen now.
why: Prior-generation resale prices easing from the scarcity peak suggests the acute shortage of that generation has passed as newer parts ship, which relieves pressure on the older installed base.

impact.mechanism: Declining resale value for the prior accelerator generation indicates easing scarcity for that vintage as buyers rotate to newer silicon, loosening the used-hardware channel.

evidence.excerpt: H100 used/refurbished traded "as high as $50,000 per GPU during mid-2024 scarcity", retail range "$25,000-$40,000 from mid-2024 into early 2026"

confidence.basis: Comparison mixes an April 2026 blog's historical ranges with today's listing snippets; different sources and methods, single secondary corroborator.

dispersion: Peak-to-present spread is wide: $50,000 at mid-2024 peak versus roughly $20,877-$27,999 asked in current listings.
